scope: Theorem 5.8 (Descent over a torus) of the manuscript “The abelianity conjecture for special compact Kähler manifolds” (preprints/The-abelianity-conjecture-for-special-compact-Kahler-manifolds-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 057 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dfbf9ad2335b9d20), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let M be a special smooth compact Kähler manifold, and let α : M → A be a surjective map to a complex torus with connected fibres. Suppose that M 99K Z g −→ A is a factorization by fibrations, and that d = dim Z − dim A > 0. On every prepared model of Z, take the inertial boundary for R = π1(M)/ Im π1(Fc) → π1(M)  , where Fc is a smooth general fibre of M 99K Z. It is impossible that, on a cofinal collection of prepared models, KY + ∆Z|Y is big for a very general g-fibre Y . The torus A is allowed to be a point.
